riepilogo:
The «turing» lab is finished. When this round began, turing.js was only a stub and turing.test.js did not exist, so I wrote both files from scratch. No other files were touched.

PURE LOGIC (exported with module.exports; no DOM access at load time):
- An immutable engine: `crea`, `passo`, `esegui` (always stops at a step limit), `contenuto`, `conta`, `valida`, `esito`, and `racconta`/`raccontoParti`, which produce the colourable step sentence in the spec's format, e.g. «Nello stato q1 leggo 1: scrivo 0, vado a sinistra, resto in q1.».
- Five programs:
  - «Somma 1»: the head runs right to the end of the number (q0), then carries leftwards (q1).
  - «Scrivi CIAO».
  - «Castoro indaffarato»: the classic 2-state, 2-symbol busy beaver table. 0 is the blank symbol. It writes 4 ones in 6 steps.
  - «Inverti i bit».
  - «Turing 1936»: Turing's first machine from the 1936 paper, with his state names b, c, e, f. It prints 0 and 1 on alternate squares and never halts.
- Helpers for the rule-editing mode: `opzioni`, `prossimo`, `stesseRegole`, `copiaRegole`.

INTERFACE (registers with ProgStoria.lab('turing', …) only when ProgStoria exists; CSS classes all start with lab-turing-):
- Layout: program selector (segmented), description, «Numero sul nastro» field (only 0 and 1, up to 10 digits; examples to try; error messages that say how to fix the input), controls bar (▶ Esegui / ⏸ Pausa / ▶ Continua / ▶ Esegui di nuovo, Passo ›, ↺ Da capo, a 5-step speed slider with an aria-valuetext label, «Passi» counter).
- The tape is a paper strip with about 15 visible cells, faded at both edges. The head shows the current state and has a green reading frame.
- Every step plays in three phases:
  1. Leggo: a light passes over the cell, the rule bar slides to the matching row and the «se» cells light up.
  2. Scrivo: the head strikes the tape, the symbol flips with an amber flash, and the written cell keeps an amber mark.
  3. Muovo: the head glides and the tape follows it with a slight lag, so the head ends up centred again; the state label rolls to the new value.
- A pulse ring on the rule bar marks the rule just used. A ▸ marks the rule that will be used next.
- The narration is coloured with fixed meanings: blue for state, white for the symbol read, amber for the symbol written, green for the head's move, pink for ALT.
- When the machine halts, a banner explains the result: the decimal check for Somma 1, the record for the busy beaver, CIAO written for Scrivi CIAO, and «Bloccata» when no rule applies. The result symbols then rise one after the other. ctx.completa() is called on ALT.
- A run that does not halt pauses itself after 100 steps (40 for Turing 1936). The banner explains why, mentions the halting problem, and the reader can continue.
- «✎ Modifica» makes Scrive, Muove and Nuovo stato into buttons that cycle through values on click, Enter, Space or arrow keys. «Ripristina» restores the original table. With an edited busy beaver the result is compared with the record, and the mirrored table ties it.
- A «Stati» panel lists the program's finite states plus ALT, highlights the current one, and shows the tape content as text.

MOTION: everything runs on ctx.anima and ctx.attendi with ctx.DURATA and ctx.EASING, and pauses offscreen. Only transform and opacity are animated, plus one CSS variable for the flash. Rapid clicks, reset, program change, edit mode or invalid input during an animation finish the current animation at once and leave the display consistent. With reduced motion every state changes instantly, and during a run the steps stay spaced out so they can be followed.

fatti.affermazione: The busy beaver game was introduced by Tibor Radó in 1962, in the paper «On Non-Computable Functions» (shown in the busy beaver's description and in the halt banner).
fatti.fonte: WebSearch: bbchallenge wiki BB(2) and Introduction to the Busy Beaver Function (https://wiki.bbchallenge.org/wiki/BB(2)); Wikipedia Busy beaver (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busy_beaver); EPFL graphsearch

fatti.affermazione: The 2-state, 2-symbol busy beaver champion is A0→1RB, A1→1LB, B0→1LA, B1→1RH. It halts at step 6 leaving 4 ones, and no 2-state machine that halts does better (Σ(2)=4, S(2)=6). The lab shows this exact table with states q0/q1 and checks it in the tests.

The first example machine in Turing's 1936 paper has m-configurations b, c, e, f: b, blank → P0, R → c; c, blank → R → e; e, blank → P1, R → f; f, blank → R → b. It prints 0 and 1 on alternate squares and never stops.

For Turing, a machine that computes a number keeps printing its digits. Machines that print infinitely many such digits are «circle-free», and computable sequences are defined through them. This is behind the description «per Turing era giusto così».
fatti.fonte: WebSearch on the text of «On Computable Numbers» (https://www.cs.virginia.edu/~robins/Turing_Paper_1936.pdf, https://people.cs.umass.edu/~immerman/cs601/TuringPaper1936.pdf)

fatti.affermazione: Turing's paper calls the machine's internal states «m-configurations»; the tape is divided into squares and the machine reads one at a time (background for state names and lab text; the term itself is not displayed).
Checked but not shown in the lab (offered for the chapter text if wanted): BB(5) = 47,176,870 steps was proved in July 2024 by the bbchallenge project with a Coq proof.

verifiche:
TESTS
- `node --test sections/programmazione/test/turing.test.js`: 16 of 16 pass.
- What they check:
  - The file loads in Node without registering itself.
  - Somma 1: 1011 → 1100 in 8 steps; 111 → 1000; +1 is correct for many numbers; leading zeros are kept.
  - Castoro indaffarato: 4 ones in 6 steps with the classic table.
  - Scrivi CIAO writes CIAO in 4 steps; Inverti i bit: 1011 → 0100.
  - Turing 1936: «0□1□0□1» after 8 steps and still running after 1000 steps.
  - A step never changes the machine it receives; a halted machine takes no further step; when no rule applies the machine is «Bloccata».
  - Every program is deterministic and has a rule for every case it meets.
  - Exact narration sentences, input validation (empty input, «2», 11 digits), and the halt texts, including an edited busy beaver and the mirrored table that ties the record.
  - Option cycling in edit mode.
- `node --test sections/programmazione/test/dati.test.js`: «capitolo 2 · logica» and «tutti i file caricati da index.html esistono» pass, with no load errors. The 7 failures are in other agents' chapters (cavi, assembly, fortran, schede, oggetti, ovunque, ia).

BROWSER (scatta.js with --hash logica --sel '[data-lab="turing"]'), 8 screenshots, each looked at
- Viewports: 1440 light, 1440 dark (edit mode on the busy beaver), 390×844 light, 320 wide with reduced motion, plus a frame taken mid-step and the busy beaver at its halt.
- Every run: errori [], risorseMancanti [], overflowOrizzontale false. The only element outside the page is the core's a.skip link.
- Click-through script (--eval), all with no console errors:
  - 10 quick clicks on Passo: 8 steps, then ALT with the correct banner.
  - Da capo during an animation.
  - Program change during a run.
  - Invalid input during a run: the run stops, aria-invalid is set, Esegui and Passo are disabled, the message reads «togli «a»». Empty input shows its own message.
  - Busy beaver, Scrivi CIAO and Inverti i bit run to ALT.
  - Turing 1936 pauses itself at 40 steps, then «Continua» works.
  - Edit mode: 12 buttons; a CIAO table edited so that no rule applies shows «Bloccata»; «Ripristina» hides itself and moves focus to «✎ Modifica»; the mirrored busy beaver ties the record.
- Offscreen pause, using instant scrolling: the step counter stays frozen while the lab is out of view and the pg-fermo class is set; it resumes when the lab returns. (With smooth scrolling across the 116,000-px page, the scroll back had not finished within my wait.)
- Keyboard and accessibility:
  - The Tab order is logical and every control is a native button or input.
  - The focus outline is 3 px green.
  - After changing a rule, focus stays on the same value button; the arrow keys cycle the value.
  - Every target is at least 40 px.
  - All lab text is at least 13 px; the only smaller text is the core's «Laboratorio» eyebrow (11.2 px).
  - Narration reaches screen readers through ctx.annuncia; ctx.completa sets «✓ esplorato».
- Reduced motion: after each Passo the head position is already a whole cell; during a run the steps stay spaced out (about 0.8 s each); the banner has no animation.
- Performance: nothing runs while idle (no endless loops or CSS animations; the ResizeObserver acts only on resize), cells far from the head are removed, and run lengths are always limited.
limiti:
- The proxy blocked direct page fetches, so the facts were checked through WebSearch results (snippets that quote the sources), not by reading the full pages.
- On narrow screens (under about 560 px) the cells keep their 38 px minimum, so about 8–10 cells are visible instead of 15. The tape still scrolls to keep the head centred.
- With smooth scrolling across this very long page, a programmatic scroll back takes more than 1.5 s. The resume itself was confirmed with instant scrolling.
- I did not test a real screen reader; I only checked the live-region texts and the ARIA attributes.
- dati.test.js still fails for 7 chapters written by other agents.
richiesteIntegratore:
- Nothing is required from the core; the lab uses only ctx and the shared classes.
- Optional: the core's `.pg-lab-eyebrow` («Laboratorio») is 11.2 px, under the 13 px minimum for text. Changing it would affect every lab, so I left it.
- Note for the chapter author (02-logica.js): the lab intro they already wrote matches the program names («Somma 1», «Castoro indaffarato», «Turing 1936») and Radó 1962. The verified BB(5) fact (47,176,870 steps, proved in 2024) is available for a «Lo sapevi?» box if wanted.
